first_impression.reaction: Googled 'average cost wedding photographer' on the train. The title literally says 'Average Wedding Photographer Cost', and the first thing I get is 'An honest answer starts with a caveat.' I kept going only to see whether a number turns up in Key Takeaways. It doesn't. I scrolled down to the FAQ to check, and the FAQ says there's no figure either. I just wanted a ballpark. The checklist of questions is useful, so I might screenshot that, but I'd go back to Google for an actual number. Not enquiring.

journey.quote: Average Wedding Photographer Cost and What Packages Include
journey.reaction: Perfect match for my search. I'm expecting a number, or at least a range.

journey.quote: An honest answer starts with a caveat.
journey.reaction: Uh oh. That's how people start when they're not going to tell you. Just tell me how much it costs.

journey.quote: A single average says very little about the quote you will receive for a wedding like yours.
journey.reaction: Fair point in theory, but I still want a rough idea so I know whether I'm looking at hundreds or thousands. Even a rough range would help.

journey.quote: A single average says little about your quote, because coverage, team, travel, products and image rights move the price far more than any national figure.
journey.reaction: Same thing again, now in the takeaways. Key Takeaways are where I expect the answer, and they repeat the caveat instead.

journey.quote: Under section 35(5) of the Copyring Act 1968, a couple who pays for wedding photos owns the copyright by default, but the agreement can change that, so read the usage clause before you sign.
journey.reaction: Copyright law wasn't my question, and it's an Australian Act. I'm in Singapore. Interesting-ish, but not why I'm here.

journey.quote: Compare quotes line by line on what is written down: hours, people, deliverables, delivery timing, licence and extras.
journey.reaction: OK, this is practical. If I can't get a price, at least I know what to compare.

journey.section: Extras that sit outside the headline package
journey.quote: The package price is the start of the conversation, not the end.
journey.reaction: Good to know. The list of extras underneath (overtime, permits, rush editing, raw files) is the kind of thing nobody warns you about. Quick to skim on a phone.

journey.quote: who books and pays for flights, transfers and car hire, and in which currency the quote is written.
journey.reaction: The currency point is actually relevant to me. Hadn't thought about that.

journey.quote: This is general information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
journey.reaction: Dated, which I like. But the whole section underneath is Australian consumer law and long Copyright Act quotes. On my phone that's a lot of scrolling for something that doesn't apply where I live. Skipping to the bottom.

journey.section: Questions to ask before you book a wedding photographer
journey.quote: Take this list into every conversation, and ask for the answers in the written quote rather than in a phone call:
journey.reaction: This is the best bit of the page for me. Clear, short questions. Screenshotting.

journey.section: How to compare quotes in writing
journey.quote: A lower headline price with fewer hours and a slower delivery date is a different product, not a saving.
journey.reaction: Fair, and a useful line to keep in mind. The numbered steps are easy to follow.

journey.quote: There is no single honest figure, because a national average blends very different weddings.
journey.reaction: The FAQ heading is my exact question and the answer is still no answer. Also it's about Australia, so even if there were a figure I'd have to convert it. This is where I give up looking for a number on this page.

journey.quote: Enough to cover what you actually want.
journey.reaction: That feels like a dodge. It's the answer a salesperson gives.

unanswered_questions: Roughly what does a wedding photographer cost? Even a broad range, or what a typical number of hours costs, would do.
How much more does it cost to fly a photographer to a destination than to book a local one?
Does any of the copyright or consumer law apply if I'm not in Australia, for example in Singapore?
Do you plan weddings for couples outside Australia, and what does Wedded Concierge cost? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: An honest answer starts with a caveat.
turn_offs_found.why: The answer I searched for is never given. The intro, Key Takeaways and FAQ all explain why there's no average, so the page doesn't do what its title says.

turn_offs_found.quote: Average Wedding Photographer Cost and What Packages Include
turn_offs_found.why: The title promises an average cost, and the page doesn't give one. It feels like clickbait, even if the reasoning is honest.

turn_offs_found.quote: Under section 35(5) of the Copyright Act 1968, a couple who pays for wedding photos owns the copyright by default, but the agreement can change that, so read the usage clause before you sign.
turn_offs_found.why: Australian legal detail takes up Key Takeaways space and a long section with blockquotes. On a phone it's a lot of scrolling past content that isn't my question and may not apply to me.

would_share_with: My fiancé: a screenshot of the 'Questions to ask before you book' list and the extras list, but I'd send a different link for the price

cta_reaction.quote: If photography is one of many suppliers you are lining up abroad, your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee with you in writing before any work begins.
cta_reaction.why: I don't know this brand, I came for a price, and the page wouldn't give me one, so I'm not about to hand over my details for a planning service. 'Quotes in AUD' also tells me it's mainly for Australians. Maybe bookmark for the checklist, not enquire.

top_3_changes: Change the title, and the FAQ heading, so they don't promise an average the page won't give (for example, lead with 'what shapes the cost' and 'what packages include'). Right now the mismatch makes the page feel like it's dodging.
Put something concrete in the first 100 words: a clear one-line answer to 'why no number', then point straight to the quote-comparison checklist, so a quick reader leaves with something useful.

Move the copyright point out of Key Takeaways and shorten the Australian legal section (link out instead of quoting the Act at length), so phone readers reach the questions list and comparison steps faster.

open_questions.question: Given the business decision to publish no prices, is a title and FAQ heading that promise an 'average' acceptable? For a search visitor the mismatch reads as a dodge and costs trust; weigh retitling against keyword targeting.

No brand facts, prices or fees invented; gaps listed as unanswered.
